selected_case.name: Netlify mock
selected_case.rationale: Fallback-repetition control with weak finding-level evidence binding and low entity ambiguity.

baseline.summary: The baseline is a sparse fallback-like payload. It is not strongly unsafe, but it repeats the same title and opening across dimensions.
baseline.primary_failure: Low information density and fallback sameness, not entity ambiguity.

shared_entity_state.entity_condition: stable enough for light state-first rewrite
shared_entity_state.state_constraint: Do not invent hidden ambiguity, contradiction, or strategic failure.

evidence_limits: The findings are fallback-like and sparse.
Brand3 should not infer full market position from the small evidence set.

can_state_as_observation: The baseline summary frames Netlify as a clear serverless/builder platform with consistent external coverage.
Evidence URLs exist for presence, perception, and vitality.
Two dimensions lack finding-level evidence URLs.
The report repeats the same fallback phrasing.
can_state_as_interpretation: The case is evidence-light at finding level, not entity-ambiguous.
State-first should improve distribution of available evidence across dimensions.
must_remain_uncertain: Whether differentiation is strong versus alternatives.
Whether the snapshot evidence is representative of the full brand.
Whether the simplified payload omits richer findings from a real run.

coordination_rules: Do not overstate differentiation where evidence is missing.
Treat missing evidence URLs as local coverage limits.

dimension_roles.coherencia: message consistency with missing local evidence
dimension_roles.percepcion: press and enterprise-facing visibility with boundaries

generated_state_first_findings.global_caveat: State-first reading treats Netlify as a stable entity. The main limitation is sparse finding-level evidence and fallback phrasing in the baseline.

coherencia.title: The core story is stable, but this finding needs local evidence
coherencia.finding: The baseline summary presents Netlify as a platform with a clear serverless/building frame and consistent external coverage. That supports a light coherence read: the report does not show competing entity narratives. However, the coherence finding itself has no evidence URL, so the claim should remain compact rather than expansive.
coherencia.confidence: medium for baseline-level coherence, lower for this local finding

presencia.title: Netlify has a legible public footprint
presencia.finding: The Wikipedia evidence supports the basic presence claim: Netlify is externally visible enough to have a public descriptive footprint. This should be treated as presence evidence, not as proof of superiority, adoption quality, or category leadership.

percepcion.title: Press and enterprise messaging support visibility, not full market validation
percepcion.finding: The TechCrunch and Netlify enterprise sources support the observation that Netlify has public and owned enterprise-facing visibility. That can strengthen perception compared with an owned-only evidence set. It should not be inflated into broad market preference or competitive dominance.

diferenciacion.title: Differentiation is plausible but under-evidenced in this payload
diferenciacion.finding: The baseline summary says Netlify is differentiated by builder experience and serverless positioning. The state-first reading keeps that as a plausible interpretation, but the finding lacks a direct evidence URL. This dimension should therefore stay cautious and avoid broad claims about alternatives.

vitalidad.title: Release activity is a safe vitality signal
vitalidad.finding: The release/blog evidence supports a narrow vitality claim: Netlify is publishing product or company updates. That is enough to say there is activity. It is not enough by itself to claim momentum, growth, or adoption.

against_baseline.specificity: State-first wins modestly by assigning a distinct job to each dimension.
against_baseline.evidence_binding: State-first wins by making missing finding-level evidence visible without repeating fallback openings.
against_baseline.entity_coherence: Baseline and state-first both preserve stable entity signal; state-first should not add ambiguity.
against_baseline.caveat_discipline: State-first wins by treating evidence scarcity as a compact limitation.
against_baseline.remaining_gap: The payload is too sparse to support deep findings.

against_watermelon.shared_pattern: Both cases benefit from evidence-boundary discipline.
against_watermelon.difference: Watermelon needed entity hierarchy; Netlify mock needs fallback compression and evidence coverage discipline.
against_watermelon.value_level: Useful but limited; this case proves state-first should not always produce a dramatic rewrite.

verdict.biggest_improvement: Repeated fallback language becomes a compact evidence-coverage limitation.
verdict.biggest_remaining_risk: State-first may invent strategic richness when the payload is too thin.
what_failed: This case does not prove the architecture in a strong real-world report.
The source payload is too sparse to support deep findings.
